Photograph: Richard Ellis/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock Climate crisis This article is more than 4 months old Ocean surface temperatures hit a record high for June This article is more than 4 months old European scientists warn of consequences for weather patterns, the global climate and marine life Jonathan Watts Wed 1 Jul 2026 03.00 BST Last modified on Wed 1 Jul 2026 03.02 BST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Temperatures on the ocean surface have hit a record high, raising fears of another burst of extreme heat this summer. On 21 June, temperatures outside the polar regions exceeded the extraordinary highs observed at the same time in 2023 and 2024, the Copernicus Climate Change Service said on Wednesday. It warned the new peak would probably bring “consequences for weather patterns, global climate and marine ecosystems”, not least because it would coincide with the earliest phases of an El Niño event they forecast to be the strongest in decades. When the previous ocean record for June was set in 2023, scientists described the trends as “worrying”, “terrifying” and “bonkers” because they were so far outside their expectations. OCED's Guide to NEPA What is NEPA? The National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) was signed into law by President Nixon on January 1, 1970, setting forth, for the first time, a national policy on the protection of the environment. The purpose of NEPA is to ensure that the federal government understands and considers the potential impact of the human environment when planning and making decisions on how to use federal resources on new projects. Video Url Ensuring that federal investments are planned and executed in a responsible, equitable, and environmentally sound manner is critically important to the U.S. Department of Energy. That’s why all projects funded by DOE’s Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations must comply with the National Environmental Policy Act — or NEPA. What do OCED awardees need to know about NEPA? There are three main types of NEPA review requiring different levels of documentation and analysis: categorical exclusion, environmental assessment, and environmental impact statement. OCED will rely on information provided by applicants, selectees, and awardees to determine what level of NEPA review is required for each project and will direct the completion of the review process. Office of Science User Facilities One important reason for establishing America’s national laboratory system immediately after World War II was to provide a home for large-scale, costly scientific facilities that universities could not afford. Such facilities were believed to be essential to sustaining America’s effort in science. The construction and operation of large-scale scientific user facilities have been integral to the mission of the DOE Office of Science from the earliest days. Today, we maintain and operate 28 DOE Office of Science user facilities at DOE national laboratories across the country as shared resources for the scientific community, with access determined on a competitive basis using peer review. Tens of thousands of researchers make use of these facilities each year. These facilities—including advanced supercomputers, particle accelerators, large x-ray light sources, neutron scattering sources, specialized facilities for nanoscience and genomics, and others—have become increasingly vital tools of scientific discovery. pages.text: Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral La Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral (Office of Labor-Management Standards, u OLMS, por sus siglas en inglés) pertenece al Departamento de Trabajo de los Estados Unidos y es responsable de administrar y aplicar la mayoría de las disposiciones de la Ley de Notificación y Divulgación Gestión Laboral (Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act, o LMRDA, por sus siglas en inglés). Dicha ley fue adoptada con el fin de garantizar normas básicas de democracia y responsabilidad fiscal en las organizaciones laborales del sector privado. Los sindicatos que representan a los empleados del Correo Postal de los Estados Unidos también se hallan sujetos a la LMRDA. Los sindicatos de empleados federales se hallan sujetos a normas similares conforme a la Ley de Reforma del Servicio Civil de 1978 (Civil Service Reform Act, o CSRA, por sus siglas in inglés) y a la Ley del Servicio Exterior de 1980. La OLMS anima a que los oficiales y los miembros del sindicato, así como otros individuos afectados por la LMRDA, se pongan en contacto con la agencia para discutir de problemas, presenten quejas u obtengan información sobre la LMRDA. Además, la OLMS fomenta la conformidad voluntaria con la LMRDA al informar a oficiales del sindicato y a otros individuos de sus responsabilidades y al animar a los miembros del sindicato a que ejerzan sus derechos. pages.text: Oldest footprints in Saudi Arabia reveal intriguing step in early human migration | National Geographic Of the hundreds of fossil footprints found at the Alathar ancient lake deposit in Saudi Arabia, scientists identified seven that were likely made by members of our own species, Homo sapiens. Photograph by Klint Janulis SCIENCE NEWS Oldest footprints in Saudi Arabia reveal intriguing step in early human migration Animal and human tracks show the lush landscape that may have greeted Homo sapiens as they ventured into new lands more than 100,000 years ago. By Maya Wei-Haas Published September 17, 2020 • 9 min read Small oval depressions—376 in all—are scattered across a patch of dry ground nestled between the dunes of northern Saudi Arabia. At a glance, these pockmarks don't seem particularly impressive, so much so that a team of scientists surveying the region almost passed them by in 2017. But upon further examination, the team realized that the depressions were left by an array of ancient animals, and among them were traces of our own species, Homo sapiens . The discovery of human footprints, if confirmed, would mark the oldest trace of our species yet found in the Arabian Peninsula, which sits at the gateway to early humans’ spread around the world. As described in a new study published in Science Advances , the frozen footfalls preserve a striking snapshot of time some 115,000 years ago, as animals and humans congregated near a shallow lake, perhaps with a shared purpose of slaking thirst and sating hunger. Currently, EFS is available for use by all LM filers: Forms LM-1, LM-2, LM-3, LM-4, LM-10, LM-15, LM-15A, LM-16, LM-20, LM-21, LM-30, and S-1, as well as simplified annual reports, filers. By accessing the OLMS EFS, you can also obtain, work on, or sign and submit an LM form. For more information on registering with EFS, see the Registration Help page . Amid calls from some victims' relatives for Dublin to commit to its own investigation, Martin said the British government's examination must be allowed to conclude first. The Omagh Bombing Inquiry is investigating whether the attack on 15 August 1998, in which 29 people including a woman pregnant with twins were killed, could have been prevented. The latest chapter in the inquiry, which is being heard in Belfast, ended this week. The next chapter is expected to begin in the new year. Martin said "two parallel inquiries at the one time, to me, never made any sense" adding that there was a need to wait for the UK government "to adjudicate on that evidence and the totality of that evidence". "We are co-operating 100% with the inquiry, and we've sent thousands of documents to the inquiry. And that to me is sensible," he told press in Dublin. National Public Lands Day brings communities together to volunteer, learn, and care for America’s shared natural and historic places. National Environmental Education Foundation (NEEF) leads national coordination and outreach, while the BLM turns that effort into on-the-ground opportunities by hosting service and educational events on BLM-managed lands. Saber wasps ( Rhyssa persuasoria ) are a large species of ichneumonid found across most of Europe. They use their ovipositor, which stretches longer than the rest of their body, to drill into wood and deposit their eggs into the insects living inside. Especially when it comes to Ichneumonidae, a family of parasitic wasps that has diversified into a dizzyingly large number of species that may dwarf the number of all known mammals, birds and fish combined . Did you know? Hurricane dangers The chaotic wind and rain produced by a hurricane is plenty scary. But the biggest risks to human life during a hurricane come from storm surges produced by that intense wind. According to the National Weather Service , storm surges and "battering waves" kill the most people during such storms, with flooding from heavy rains causing the second highest numbrer of deaths. pages.text: One thing Hollywood gets right about Ancient Rome | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE One thing Hollywood gets right about Ancient Rome Gladiators really were sex symbols—just not in the way one might expect. Gladiators were ancient Roman sex symbols Rebecca Hale, National Geographic By Harry Sidebottom Published July 24, 2026 Hollywood is often criticized for getting history wrong, rarely more so than in films about Rome . One could take issue with the lack of color, whether in the robes that clothe posh-sounding British actors or the statues and other works in marble stripped of their polychromy. In arguably the most famous movie about Rome, Gladiator , inaccuracies abound, from puzzling choices in how the gladiators are armed to the tigers released to endanger the combatants. Credulity is strained even further in the sequel when a naval fight is recreated in the Colosseum (which could not be flooded by the period in which the film is set) and great white sharks devour those who fall into the water. The heights of physical impossibility are reached when a gladiator rides a rhinoceros, complete with saddle and stirrups, into the arena. But there is one thing Hollywood gets right. Gladiators were ancient Roman sex symbols, although not in the way one might expect, or that Hollywood portrays. (Who really built Rome?) As the graffiti etched into barracks in Pompeii capture, gladiators saw themselves as sex symbols.
